planted.detail: and he said that she should be given something to eat
, just as he had promised long before
twelve -> ten

findings.english: and they were afraid, just as he had promised long before.
findings.problem: The clause "just as he had promised long before" has no basis in the Greek, which simply says they were afraid.

findings.english: for she was ten years old
findings.problem: The Greek says the girl was twelve years old, not ten.

findings.english: He gave them strict orders that no one should know about this.
findings.problem: The English omits the final clause, Jesus' instruction that she be given something to eat.

planted.detail: for I have found the drachma that I lost
, and all who heard of it were amazed
heaven -> earth

findings.greek: ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα
findings.english: ‘Rejoice with me.’
findings.problem: The reason clause, 'for I have found the drachma that I had lost,' is missing from the English.

findings.english: I have sinned against earth
findings.problem: οὐρανός means 'heaven', not 'earth'. The English reverses the meaning and breaks the echo of v18.

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: The Greek ends with 'they began to celebrate'. The clause about all who heard being amazed has no basis in the text.

planted.detail: because they see the light of this world
, though none of them understood it
death -> life

findings.greek: ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει
findings.english: they do not stumble.
findings.problem: The causal clause "because they see the light of this world" is missing from the English.

findings.english: about his life
findings.problem: The Greek says Jesus had been speaking about Lazarus's death, not his life.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The Greek has no clause saying that none of them understood; this is added content.

planted.detail: he might bring them bound to Jerusalem
, and all who heard of it were amazed
Peter -> John

findings.english: men or women.
findings.problem: The purpose clause 'he might bring them bound to Jerusalem' is missing, which leaves the sentence incomplete and drops Saul's stated aim.

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: The amazement of the hearers belongs to verse 21, where it is already rendered. Verse 20's Greek does not contain it.

findings.english: But John sent them all outside
findings.problem: The Greek names Peter, not John, as the one who sent everyone out.

planted.detail: because he intercedes for the holy ones in accordance with God’s will
, though none of them understood it
death -> life

findings.greek: ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων
findings.english: knows what the mindset of the Spirit is.
findings.problem: The clause stating that the Spirit intercedes for the holy ones according to God has no counterpart in the English.

findings.english: we are being put to life
findings.problem: θανατούμεθα means "we are being put to death". The English reverses the meaning.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The Greek has nothing corresponding to this added clause.

planted.detail: just as I have also been fully known
, though none of them understood it
faith -> hope

findings.english: all hope
findings.problem: πίστις means faith, not hope. The English has the wrong word, which also blurs the faith/hope/love triad in v. 13.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The clause "though none of them understood it" has no basis in the Greek and has been added.

findings.english: but then I will know fully.
findings.problem: The clause "just as I also have been fully known" is missing from the English.

planted.detail: so that what is seen did not come into being from things that appear
, and all who heard of it were amazed
faith -> hope

findings.greek: εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὸ βλεπόμενον γεγονέναι
findings.english: By faith we understand that the worlds were set in order by God’s word.
findings.problem: The result clause, 'so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible', has no counterpart in the English.

findings.english: By hope
findings.problem: The Greek says 'by faith' (πίστει), the refrain of the chapter, not 'by hope'.

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: Nothing in the Greek says that those who heard were amazed. The clause is added.

planted.detail: so that he can open the scroll and its seven seals
, just as he had promised long before
heaven -> earth

findings.greek: Τίς ἄξιος ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ λῦσαι τὰς σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ;
findings.english: just as he had promised long before?
findings.problem: The clause "just as he had promised long before" has no basis in the Greek and changes the meaning of the angel's question.

findings.english: in earth
findings.problem: The Greek says "in heaven", but the English has "in earth", which loses the heaven/earth/under-earth triad.

findings.greek: ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ
findings.english: has conquered.”
findings.problem: The purpose of the conquest, "so as to open the scroll and its seven seals", is omitted.

findings.english: said
findings.problem: The present tense λέγει ("says") is rendered as a past tense. This is a common historical-present smoothing and has little effect on meaning.

findings.english: sent out into all the earth
findings.problem: This is rendered adequately, so there is no real problem here.
